intermediate_mechanisms: OL dysfunction and myelin abnormalities impair neural plasticity through loss of metabolic and trophic support to neurons.
OL-microglia and OL-astrocyte interactions link oligodendrocyte dysfunction to neuroinflammatory signaling in MDD.

Fewer newborn neuroblasts with reduced doublecortin and BDNF lower the rate at which new granule cells are added to the dentate gyrus, reducing structural and synaptic plasticity of the trisynaptic circuit.
Interferon-stimulated gene expression in stem cells and progenitors is proposed to restrain their progression, but the study is cross-sectional and does not establish the direction of this edge.

Stage-specific transcription factors, including the stress-responsive KLF9 acting at the intermediate-progenitor to neuroblast transition, set the chromatin accessibility and gene expression that the neurogenic trajectory depends on.
KLF15 footprint changes in CA1-4 excitatory and PENK+ inhibitory neurons track expression of synaptic target genes including HOMER1, CAMKV and RAB6B.

An activated PENK+ inhibitory population alongside downregulated ionotropic and metabotropic glutamate receptors in dentate granule and neurogenic cells shifts the excitatory-inhibitory balance of the dentate gyrus, but whether the inhibitory activation is cause or compensation is undetermined.

edges.description: Supplies a human-cell assay for the activation state of the cell type the node names, and resolves it by stimulus rather than treating activation as one condition. The microglia-to-astrocyte arm addresses the same crosstalk that the entry's P2rx7/Il6/Il6ra mouse model proposes, in human cells and with a different mediator.
edges.limitations: Monoculture of one cell type, with astrocytes reached only through transferred medium; no neurons, no vasculature, no tissue context. The stimuli are pathogen-associated or cytokine challenges, not the chronic stress the node's upstream causes imply, and nothing links any state to an affective outcome. iPSC-derived microglia-like cells are not shown here to match adult human microglia in situ.
edges.source: iPSC-derived microglia-like cells under diverse inflammogens

edges.description: Applies an inflammatory challenge to human brain tissue containing both microglia and neurons, and isolates the microglial contribution by comparing organoids that have them against ones that do not. That comparison is the model's distinctive capability and is not available in the entry's other models for this node.
edges.limitations: The study is about prenatal immune challenge and neurodevelopmental disorder risk, not depression; its outcome genes are autism-linked. The organoid is a developing cortical tissue with no hippocampal specification, no vasculature and no adaptive immune input, and the challenge is a single cytokine rather than chronic stress.

edges.description: Manipulates the exact step the node names: corticosteroid control of KLF9 in hippocampal neurons. It establishes the regulation as direct and maps the cis-elements and the chromatin events through which it acts, which is the mechanism the node's footprinting data can only infer.
edges.limitations: An immortalised mouse line, so cell identity, chromatin state and ploidy are not those of human hippocampal neurons, and the node's cell-type resolution - granule cells, CA1-4 excitatory neurons, PENK+ inhibitory neurons - cannot be represented at all. KLF15, EGR and ASCL1, also named in the node, are not addressed. The node describes altered transcription-factor binding activity in disease; this model shows normal hormonal regulation of one factor.
edges.source: HT-22 hippocampal cell line, corticosterone induction of Klf9

edges.description: Puts an interferon response signature and a defined neural-stem-cell quiescence state in the same cells, which is the pairing the node asserts from human post-mortem data. It makes the association manipulable: quiescence state here is set experimentally rather than observed.
edges.limitations: In this system the interferon signature is a marker of a normal primed quiescent state, not a disease-associated activation, so the model supplies the association without the pathology. It is mouse subventricular zone, not human hippocampus, and the node's specific genes (EIF2AK2, IFIT3, HERC6, NRIR, IFITM3, MX1) are not the ones reported here. NRIR has no mouse ortholog, being a human long non-coding RNA. The node also records the interferon programme as raised in mature granule cells and CA1-4 excitatory neurons, which this model does not contain.
edges.source: Primed quiescent neural stem cell culture with an interferon response signature

edges.description: Informative by analogy only. It is the available experimental handle on what turns proenkephalin transcription up and down in a GABAergic neuron, and it identifies the controlling inputs - NMDA receptor drive, opposed by GABA-A signalling on the same cells. The node's population overexpresses proenkephalin alongside immediate-early genes in what the authors read as an activated state, and NMDA-driven activation opposed by local inhibition is a candidate mechanism for that. The cell the node names is not present in this system.
edges.limitations: Wrong cell, wrong region, wrong species. The node's population is a PENK+ medium-spiny-neuron-like GABAergic interneuron in human hippocampus, not previously described there; this is a GABAergic projection neuron in rat neostriatum. PENK+ medium spiny neurons are well described in rodent striatum, and that resemblance is what licenses the analogy at all; what the search behind this record did not find is a report of a hippocampal PENK+ interneuron population in a model species. So the model cannot recapitulate the node under any reading. It is recorded as the proenkephalin regulatory precedent, and should not be cited as a model of the node.
edges.source: Rat neostriatal slice culture, proenkephalin gene regulation

edges.description: Reproduces the serotonin-loss half of the node, with complete rather than reduced loss, and shows one downstream consequence the node does not name: de-repression of a FOXO stress transcription factor through reduced insulin-receptor signalling. It says nothing about norepinephrine or dopamine, and nothing about brain circuits.
edges.limitations: The node describes reduced serotonin, norepinephrine and dopamine transmission in human brain circuits. The worm has no norepinephrine, the model abolishes serotonin rather than reducing it, and the readouts are DAF-16 localisation, feeding, egg laying and fat storage, none of which is a mood or reward measure. The FOXO consequence has no counterpart node in this entry, so the link records a mechanism the entry does not yet model.

edges.description: Offers a whole-animal behavioural state, loss of goal-directed foraging that antidepressants and clozapine reverse, as a distant proxy for the diminished motivation and anhedonia the node explains. The node's own content, an elevated and inflexible decisional reference point in anterior cingulate cortex, has no counterpart in the worm.
edges.limitations: Foraging immobility is the only readout. There is no reward valuation, no reference point and no cortex, so the node's mechanism is not tested, only a behavioural endpoint that could plausibly sit downstream of it. The authors attribute the immobility to excess serotonergic and cholinergic signalling, the opposite direction from the entry's Monoamine Deficiency node, which is why this model is not linked there. Drug reversal is by tricyclics and atypical antipsychotics; SSRIs were not reported in the abstract.
edges.source: daf-2 insulin-receptor loss-of-function immobility C. elegans

edges.description: Wild-type mice under social defeat show a stress-induced fall in synaptic serotonin through increased transporter-mediated uptake, the serotonin arm of the node. Deleting p38alpha in serotonergic neurons removes that step and the behavioural consequence, so the model perturbs one upstream route into the node rather than reproducing the node as a whole.
edges.limitations: The node covers serotonin, norepinephrine and dopamine; the model addresses serotonin uptake only. The behavioural readout is social avoidance after defeat, not a measure of human depressed mood. A p38 inhibitor, losmapimod, showed no antidepressant advantage in the larger of two human MDD trials (PMID:24699061, cited in the MAPK14 knowledge gap), so the pathway's role in people is unconfirmed.
edges.source: Serotonergic-neuron p38alpha MAPK conditional knockout mouse under social defeat

edges.description: Astrocytic Fgf13 loss raises inflammation and overexpression lowers it, so the model moves the node in both directions. It reaches the node through astrocyte apoptosis, a route the entry records only as an emerging hypothesis and not as a pathophysiology node.
edges.limitations: The node is defined by elevated inflammatory cytokines in people with depression; the model reports inflammation secondary to astrocyte death in mouse hippocampus. Human support for the astrocytic FGF13 chain is a secondary transcriptomic association in an all-male suicide cohort, and earlier biochemistry favoured p38delta rather than JNK downstream of JIP2. These points are set out in the entry's FGF13 human-model mismatch discussion, which this model attaches to.
edges.source: Astrocyte-specific Fgf13 knockout and overexpression mouse under chronic stress

edges.description: Reproduces an inflammasome-driven inflammatory process in the stressed brain and shows by genetic loss of three of its components that the process contributes to the behavioural phenotype.
edges.limitations: The node is defined by elevated inflammatory cytokines in people with depression; the model measures inflammasome and pyroptosis proteins in mouse astrocytes under chronic mild stress. Astrocyte pyroptosis has not been shown in human MDD tissue, and the entry's FGF13 mismatch discussion records human hippocampal astrocyte findings that are region-, sex- and medication-dependent.
edges.source: Gsdmd, Casp1 and astrocytic Nlrp3 knockout mice under chronic mild stress

edges.description: Reproduces raised IL-6, one of the cytokines the node names, together with microglial activation, and shows by cell-type-selective knockdown that microglial IL-6 acting on astrocytes contributes to the behavioural phenotype.
edges.limitations: The node rests on elevated inflammatory cytokines in people with depression; the model measures microglial IL-6 in the mouse hippocampus. Its downstream target, astrocyte apoptosis, is not a node in this entry, and human evidence for hippocampal astrocyte loss is mixed, as the entry's FGF13 mismatch discussion records.
edges.source: Microglial P2rx7 and Il6 and astrocytic Il6ra knockdown mice under chronic social defeat stress

edges.description: Ablates the cell type the node names and reproduces the demyelination step directly, by killing myelinating glia rather than by any disease-related route. Its distinctive contribution is the recovery phase: the node proposes therapeutic remyelination as a target, and this model measures remyelination on a defined timetable.
edges.limitations: The lesion is acute, synchronous and toxin-driven, where the node describes chronic dysfunction arising from stress, inflammation and impaired metabolic support. The model carries none of those upstream causes, and reports no conduction, connectivity or behavioural consequence.

edges.description: Reaches the consequence the node asserts but does not itself demonstrate: that impaired myelination reduces conduction velocity and disrupts circuit function. The mutants supply both measurements in the same animal, at single-axon resolution and with a behavioural output.
edges.limitations: Hypomyelination here is developmental and genetic, never established and then lost, so the model says nothing about demyelination of a myelinated tract. The behavioural readout is a sensorimotor startle decision, not an affective measure, and the node's inflammatory and metabolic-support arms are untouched.

edges.description: Produces the node's elevated-cortisol state and ties it to a persistent, non-habituating behavioural phenotype that antidepressant treatment reverses. The teleost hypothalamic-pituitary-interrenal axis is the homologue of the mammalian HPA axis, and the receptor the node's mechanism runs through is the one disrupted.
edges.limitations: Cortisol is elevated here because feedback is broken at the receptor, so no tissue can respond to it. The node describes axis hyperactivity with receptor signalling intact, which is a different state: the mutant cannot show glucocorticoid-driven hippocampal atrophy, because the glucocorticoid cannot act. The hippocampal-atrophy and cognitive arms of the node are therefore out of reach, and the fish has no hippocampus proper.

edges.description: Puts glial inflammatory marker expression, stress duration and affective behaviour on the same axis in one experiment, which is what the node asserts a relationship between. Its result partly contradicts the node: the pro-inflammatory profile travelled with the anxiety-like five-week state, and the depression-like twelve-week state came with anti-inflammatory markers and lowered cortisol.
edges.limitations: The readouts are marker gene expression in whole brain, not cytokine protein in the cell types the node names, and the node's human markers (IL-6, TNF-alpha, CRP) are not among them. Behaviour is scored on zebrafish anxiety and depression-like assays. The dissociation between stress duration and inflammatory polarity is a single-study result and is recorded here as such.
edges.source: Adult zebrafish chronic unpredictable stress, 5 and 12 weeks

nodes.description: Adult zebrafish exposed to five or twelve weeks of chronic unpredictable stress, assayed for behaviour, whole-body cortisol, brain monoamines, blood-brain-barrier permeability and a panel of pro- and anti-inflammatory microglial and astroglial marker genes. The two durations dissociate: five weeks produced anxiety-like behaviour with raised pro-inflammatory markers, cortisol signalling and norepinephrine, while twelve weeks produced depression-like behaviour with lowered cortisol, impaired serotonin turnover and activation of anti-inflammatory markers instead.
nodes.id: Adult zebrafish chronic unpredictable stress, 5 and 12 weeks

nodes.description: In mouse depression models, FGF13 falls, mainly in astrocytes, alongside hippocampal astrocyte apoptosis and lower synaptic protein levels. Removing Fgf13 from astrocytes increases astrocyte apoptosis and inflammation and worsens depression-like behaviour; overexpressing it reduces all three. The proposed mechanism is FGF13 binding and inhibiting JIP2, which blocks JIP2-JNK signalling and Bax/Bcl-2-mediated apoptosis. The paper's figure legends name chronic restraint stress for the stress-induced phenotypes and chronic social defeat stress for the knockout and overexpression arms. They are recorded in prose because AnimalModel has no slot for a non-genetic perturbation (#13768). This is the model behind the entry's emerging astrocytic FGF13-JIP2-JNK cell-death hypothesis.
nodes.id: Astrocyte-specific Fgf13 knockout and overexpression mouse under chronic stress

evidence.reference_title: FGF13 alleviates astrocytic apoptosis via JIP2 inhibition in the hippocampus and mitigates depression-like behavior.
evidence.snippet: In depressive models, FGF13 expression is markedly reduced, particularly in astrocytes, accompanied by astrocyte apoptosis in the hippocampal region and decreased synaptic protein levels in the nervous system.

evidence.reference_title: FGF13 alleviates astrocytic apoptosis via JIP2 inhibition in the hippocampus and mitigates depression-like behavior.
evidence.snippet: Mechanistically, FGF13 directly binds to JIP2 protein, inhibits its activity, and subsequently blocks the downstream JIP2-JNK signaling pathway, thereby suppressing Bax/Bcl-2-mediated astrocyte apoptosis.

nodes.description: Cerebral organoids with microglia integrated into them, built to study prenatal immune challenge. The organoids express microglial markers and respond to inflammatory stimuli. Microglial presence alters organoid development itself - cell density, neural differentiation, and ciliated and mesenchymal marker expression - and organoids with and without microglia respond to inflammatory stimuli both similarly and distinctly. Interferon-gamma produced transcriptional and structural change that depended on microglia being present, including altered expression of autism-linked genes.
Most effective treatment for severe or treatment-resistant depression.

Reduced cortex-wide excitation-inhibition (E/I) balance in prefrontal-cingulate cortices, reflecting dysregulation of GABAergic inhibitory and glutamatergic excitatory neurotransmission. E/I imbalance is implicated in depressive symptoms and ketamine treatment response in treatment-resistant depression.

evidence.snippet: Patients with MDD demonstrated significantly reduced Hurst exponent values, predominantly encompassing the parietal and prefrontal-cingulate cortices.

nodes.description: A zebrafish mutant that survives to adulthood with no GR transcriptional activity. Negative feedback on the stress axis is lost and cortisol is elevated but inert at GR. In an unfamiliar tank the mutants freeze, explore less and fail to habituate on repeated exposure. Fluoxetine in the holding water, and social interaction, restore the behaviour, with cortisol correcting later; fluoxetine does not change baseline transcription of CRH, MR, the serotonin transporter or GR, but suppresses their stress-induced upregulation. The authors offer it as a platform for high-throughput antidepressant screening.

Mice under chronic mild stress show astrocytic pyroptosis, an inflammatory cell death driven by the NLRP3 inflammasome, caspase-1 and gasdermin D, and the pyroptosis accounts for their astrocyte loss. An SSRI reduces it. Knocking out Gsdmd, Casp1 or astrocytic Nlrp3 reduces depression-like behaviour and pyroptosis-associated proteins, and restoring the active GSDMD fragment in astrocytes removes the protection. Chronic mild stress is recorded in prose because AnimalModel has no slot for a non-genetic perturbation (#13768).
nodes.id: Gsdmd, Casp1 and astrocytic Nlrp3 knockout mice under chronic mild stress

nodes.description: The mouse hippocampal line HT-22 treated with corticosterone, used to establish how glucocorticoid drives Krueppel-like factor 9. Induction was time- and dose-dependent and survived protein synthesis inhibition, marking Klf9 as a direct glucocorticoid-response gene. Two GR/MR response elements were located at -6.1 and -5.3 kb and verified by enhancer-reporter, gel shift and chromatin immunoprecipitation; GR recruitment, histone hyperacetylation and nucleosome removal were seen at those regions. The -5.3 kb element is largely conserved across tetrapods, while orthologs of the -6.1 kb element were detected only in therian mammals.

nodes.description: Early neurogenic stages in the MDD hippocampus - quiescent and activated neural stem cells and intermediate neural progenitors - upregulate a gene module enriched for interferon-related pathways (EIF2AK2, IFIT3, HERC6, NRIR, IFITM3, MX1). nodes.description: Oligodendrocyte (OL) dysfunction and myelin abnormalities contribute to depression pathophysiology through multiple mechanisms: impaired myelination reduces conduction velocity and disrupts neural circuit function; loss of OL-derived metabolic support decreases neuronal energy supply; compromised OL-glial crosstalk with microglia and astrocytes amplifies neuroinflammation. These dysfunctions are associated with altered brain connectivity and emotional processing deficits, and may represent a targetable node for therapeutic remyelination strategies.

animal_models.category: Inducible cell-ablation model of demyelination and remyelination
animal_models.description: Ablates the cell type the node names and reproduces the demyelination step directly, by killing myelinating glia rather than by any disease-related route. Its distinctive contribution is the recovery phase: the node proposes therapeutic remyelination as a target, and this model measures remyelination on a defined timetable.
animal_models.genotype: Tg(mbp:mCherry-NTR); bacterial nitroreductase driven by the myelin basic protein promoter, so myelinating glia are selectively killed on metronidazole treatment. Not a mutant; ablation is drug-inducible and reversible.

evidence.snippet: Emerging evidence increasingly implicates oligodendrocyte (OL) dysfunction as a key pathophysiological mechanism in MDD, extending beyond their classical role in myelination to include critical contributions to neural plasticity, metabolic support, and circuit regulation.

nodes.description: A PENK+ medium-spiny-neuron-like GABAergic population, not previously described in the human hippocampus, is the most transcriptionally dysregulated cell cluster in MDD. It overexpresses proenkephalin together with immediate-early genes (ARC, FOS, JUNB, EGRs, JAG1) and shows altered vesicle, dendritic-spine and adhesion genes plus elevated HTR1D, a profile the authors read as an activated state possibly compensating for a stress-hyperactivated dentate gyrus. It is offered as a link between MDD, chronic pain, stress response and emotional regulation.

The node's population overexpresses proenkephalin alongside immediate-early genes in what the authors read as an activated state, and NMDA-driven activation opposed by local inhibition is a candidate mechanism for that. nodes.description: Adult mouse neural stem cells driven into two distinct quiescent states in culture: BMP-4 alone gives a dormant non-cycling state, while BMP-4 with FGF-2 gives a primed state poised to re-enter the cell cycle. The primed state is defined by high LRIG1 and CD9 together with an interferon response signature, and engrafts efficiently into the adult subventricular zone niche. LRIG1 is the functional gatekeeper: disrupting Lrig1 in subventricular zone stem cells in vivo increases proliferation, and LRIG1 works by letting EGFR protein accumulate while limiting its signalling.

Participants received 25-mg psilocybin or placebo with preparation, dosing support and integration.

nodes.description: Organotypic slice cultures of rat neostriatum used to work out what controls proenkephalin gene expression. In the neostriatum the gene is expressed in medium spiny GABA neurons projecting to the globus pallidus, and its expression is driven by glutamatergic input through NMDA receptors. The cultures showed that GABA released from neostriatal neurons negatively regulates NMDA-driven proenkephalin expression, that the GABA-A receptors responsible appear to be colocalised with NMDA receptors on the same projection neurons, and that intrinsic striatal and thalamic glutamatergic afferents drive the gene as well as cortical ones.

nodes.description: Pathological elevation and inflexibility of the decisional reference point, a core mechanism from behavioral economics that determines how events are experienced as positive or negative. Elevated reference points cause previously rewarding activities to be experienced as aversive, contributing to anhedonia and reward dysfunction. Dysfunction in anterior cingulate cortex impairs dynamic adjustment of the reference point to environmental changes.

nodes.description: Wild-type mice exposed to social defeat stress develop social avoidance and reinstate cocaine preference; mice lacking p38alpha MAPK in dorsal raphe serotonergic neurons do neither. In wild-type animals, stress activates p38alpha, which moves the serotonin transporter to the plasma membrane and raises serotonin uptake at serotonergic terminals. The authors read this as a stress-induced hyposerotonergic state. Social defeat itself is a procedure applied to the animals, recorded here in prose because AnimalModel has no slot for a non-genetic perturbation (#13768).

In nonmedicated MDD, the subgranular-zone (SGZ) neurogenic lineage of the dentate gyrus shows a shift in pseudotime distribution toward quiescent neural stem cells with fewer neuroblasts, indicating arrested progression rather than depletion of the stem-cell pool. Histological validation finds fewer nestin- and Ki67-expressing SGZ cells and fewer DCX/TUBB3 co-expressing dentate cells, while the immature granule-cell (ImGC2) pool is unchanged. Intermediate progenitors upregulate SOX9, favouring a neuron-to-glia switch, and the residual neuroblasts lose doublecortin and BDNF.

nodes.description: A transgenic zebrafish line in which nitroreductase expressed from the mbp promoter converts the prodrug metronidazole into a cytotoxic metabolite, killing myelinating glia on demand. A two-day treatment removes about two-thirds of oligodendrocytes; demyelination follows a week later and remyelination is observed by sixteen days. The line was built to image cell behaviour through a demyelination-remyelination cycle and to screen genetic or chemical modifiers of it. It is not a depression model and has no affective readout: it supplies the oligodendrocyte-loss and myelin-repair arm of the node in a system where both can be watched in a living animal.
Non-invasive neuromodulation for treatment-resistant depression.

Loss-of-function mutations in the insulin receptor daf-2 make non-dauer adult worms immobile. The animals still respond to external stimuli but do not forage and stay in place for more than 12 days or until they die. The same immobility is produced without a mutation, by brief food deprivation or DMSO exposure, and by syntaxin unc-64 loss of function; only the daf-2 genotype is recorded here because AnimalModel has no slot for a non-genetic perturbation (see #13754). Amitriptyline, amoxapine, clozapine and olanzapine prevent the immobility; benzodiazepines and haloperidol do not. Recovery experiments attribute the state to excessive serotonergic and muscarinic cholinergic signalling. The authors present the immobility as a potential protophenotype for avolition and anhedonia. It is a foraging assay in a nematode, not a measure of mood or reward, and it should not be read as modelling human anhedonia.

evidence.reference_title: Insulin Signaling Deficiency Produces Immobility in Caenorhabditis elegans That Models Diminished Motivation States in Man and Responds to Antidepressants.
evidence.snippet: We have discovered that loss-of-function mutations in the insulin receptor (daf-2) and syntaxin (unc-64) genes in Caenorhabditis elegans, brief food deprivation, and exposure to DMSO produce immobility and avolition in non-dauer adults. The animals remain responsive to external stimuli; however, they fail to forage and will remain in place for >12 days or until they die.

evidence.reference_title: Insulin Signaling Deficiency Produces Immobility in Caenorhabditis elegans That Models Diminished Motivation States in Man and Responds to Antidepressants.
evidence.snippet: Recovery experiments confirm that immobility is induced and maintained by excessive signaling via serotonergic and muscarinic cholinergic pathways.

nodes.description: Microglia-like cells differentiated from human iPSCs, validated by transcriptome profiling against microglial signature genes, then mapped across inflammatory states by stimulating them with cytokines and with agonists of four Toll-like receptors. Each stimulus gave a distinguishable morphology, cytokine secretion profile and transcriptional signature, and engaged NF-kB or JAK-STAT signalling selectively. Supernatants from microglia stimulated with FSL-1, LPS or Poly(I:C) activated astrocytes, and that propagation was strictly dependent on TNF-alpha.

nodes.description: Zebrafish carrying mutations in myelin regulatory factor myelinate the CNS poorly. The mutants are slower to start an acoustic startle response and often substitute a reorientation for the stimulus-appropriate startle. Single-axon recordings show reduced action-potential conduction velocity and a failure to sustain high-frequency firing. The study's purpose was to establish that myelination in larval zebrafish can be tied to circuit function, which is what makes the line usable for this node rather than for myelin biology alone.

Caenorhabditis elegans has one tryptophan hydroxylase gene. Animals carrying a tph-1 deletion make no serotonin, stay viable, feed and lay eggs less, store fat, and sometimes arrest as dauers. Under stress they show nuclear accumulation of DAF-16, the worm FOXO transcription factor, and constitutive physiological stress states, as insulin-receptor daf-2 mutants do. Exogenous serotonin and fluoxetine prevent that nuclear accumulation in wild-type animals under stress, and genetic analysis places the insulin receptor downstream of serotonin. The model removes one monoamine completely; it has no behavioural depression readout and is not a model of the disease.

evidence.reference_title: Food and metabolic signalling defects in a Caenorhabditis elegans serotonin-synthesis mutant.
evidence.snippet: Analysis of the C. elegans genome sequence showed that there is a single tryptophan hydroxylase gene (tph-1)-the key enzyme for serotonin biosynthesis. Animals bearing a tph-1 deletion mutation do not synthesize serotonin but are fully viable.

evidence.reference_title: Food and metabolic signalling defects in a Caenorhabditis elegans serotonin-synthesis mutant.
evidence.snippet: The tph-1 mutant shows abnormalities in behaviour and metabolism that are normally coupled with the sensation and ingestion of food: rates of feeding and egg laying are decreased; large amounts of fat are stored; reproductive lifespan is increased; and some animals arrest at the metabolically inactive dauer stage.

evidence.reference_title: Serotonin targets the DAF-16/FOXO signaling pathway to modulate stress responses.
evidence.snippet: Exogenous 5HT and fluoxetine (Prozac) prevented DAF-16 nuclear accumulation in wild-type animals under stresses.
